message.content:
Below are three common ways to pull **all node‑level data** for a fabric called *“test‑de”*.  
Pick whichever fits your environment best – whether you’re working against an APIC/ACI controller, a plain NX‑OS switch, or a scripted automation framework.

---

### 1️⃣  REST API against the APIC (Cisco ACI)

If *23.31.32.1* is the IP of your APIC controller, you can query its CMDB for all nodes belonging to the “test‑de” fabric.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
APIC="https://23.31.32.1"
USER="admin"
PASS="your_password"

# Get CSRF token first
TOKEN=$(curl -sk "$APIC/api/aaaLogin.xml" \
    --data "<aaaUser><attributes><name>$USER</name><pwd>$PASS</pwd></attributes></aaaUser>" |
        xmllint --xpath "//imdata[0]/aaaToken/text()" - )

# Query all nodes in the fabric
curl -sk -H "Cookie:$TOKEN" \
     "$APIC/api/node/class/fabricNode.json?$filter=fabric.name==\"test-de\"" > nodes_test_de.json
```

> **What it returns:**  
> An array of objects each containing:
> ```json
> {
>   "dn": "uni/fabric/test-de/nodes-[101]",
>   "id": 101,
>   "role": "leaf",
>   "ipAddress": "10.100.20.101",
>   ...
> }
> ```

#### Quick one‑liner with `jq`
```bash
cat nodes_test_de.json | jq '.imdata[]|{dn:.fvTenant.attributes.dn,id:.fvTenant.attributes.id}'
```

---

### 2️⃣  CLI on a Nexus Switch (NX‑OS)  

On a single switch that’s part of the fabric, you can dump the entire configuration tree and filter out the relevant parts.

```bash
ssh admin@23.31.32.1
switch(config)# terminal length 0          # avoid paging
switch# show running-config | grep '^hostname'      # quick sanity check
switch# show lldp neighbors detail              # see peers
switch# show platform hardware status            # node health
```

For a full snapshot:

```bash
switch# copy running-config tftp://<tftpd-host>/nodes-test-de.cfg
```

Then parse the file locally (`grep`, `awk`, `sed`) to extract node names/IPs/etc.

---

### 3️⃣  Automation Script (Python + Netmiko/CiscoSDK)

Using the official Cisco SDK gives you typed access to the same APIs as above, plus convenient error handling.

```python
from netmiko import ConnectHandler
import json

device = {
    'device_type': 'cisco_nxos',
    'host': '23.31.32.1',
    'username': 'admin',
    'password': 'your_pass',
}

with ConnectHandler(**device) as ssh:
    output = ssh.send_command('show running-config')
    print(output[:500])           # preview

# If you prefer the REST API route:
import requests, urllib3
urllib3.disable_warnings()
url = f"https://23.31.32.1/api/node/class/fabricNode.json?$filter=fabric.name=='test-de'"
resp = requests.get(url, auth=('admin','your_pass'), verify=False)
print(json.dumps(resp.json(), indent=2))
```

---

## Which method to pick?

| Scenario | Recommended Approach |
|----------|----------------------|
| You have direct SSH/Telnet into the switches | CLI & local parsing |
| You own an APIC/APIC‑SP controller | REST API (or SDK) |
| You’re writing automated tests or integrations | Python SDK / Netmiko |

Feel free to let me know which path you’ll take, and I can drill down further—e.g., exact JSON fields, filtering tips, or converting the data into CSV/Pandas DataFrames!
